title: Second Largest
problem: The first line of input is a positive integer N. The second line holds N integers separated by spaces. Print the second largest distinct value: the largest value that is smaller than the maximum. If there is no such value, print "None". For example, in 5 9 9 3 the largest is 9 and the second largest distinct value is 5.
starter_code:
# The first line is N, the count of numbers.
# The second line holds N integers separated by spaces.
# Print the largest value that is smaller than the maximum,
# or "None" if there isn't one.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Repeats of the largest value do not count as a second largest. Think about removing repeats first.
hints.2: Turn the numbers into a set to drop repeats, then sort it. If only one distinct value is left, the answer is None; otherwise it is the second value from the top.
hints.3:
input()
values = sorted(set(map(int, input().split())))
print(values[-2] if len(values) > 1 else 'None')

failure_explanation: The second largest must be strictly smaller than the largest, so repeats of the maximum have to be skipped: taking the second item of a sorted list picks the maximum again when it appears twice. Print None when only one distinct value exists, including a list with a single number, and compare the values as numbers so negative numbers work too.
